repo_map.purpose: Click is a Python library for building command-line interfaces. It is composable: commands, groups, options and arguments are built from decorators or classes. It handles parsing, help generation, prompts, shell completion and testing.
repo_map.intended_users: Python developers writing CLI applications. Maintainers and contributors working on Pallets/Click itself.

repo_map.execution_flow: Command.main (core.py:1483) takes args from sys.argv[1:], expanding globs on Windows via _expand_args, or from the args you pass. It detects the program name and calls _main_shell_completion (line 1619). If the _<PROG>_COMPLETE env var is set, that function runs shell_complete and exits. Otherwise main opens `with self.make_context(prog_name, args, **extra) as ctx` and calls self.invoke(ctx). make_context calls parse_args. For each parameter, parse_args calls Parameter.handle_parse_result (core.py:2763), which does the following: consume_value picks a value and a ParameterSource; a deprecation warning is echoed to stderr if the value was set explicitly; process_value runs type conversion and callbacks; then the value is stored in ctx.params, with arbitration when several parameters share one name. Group.invoke dispatches to subcommands through resolve_command (core.py:2088). In standalone mode main then calls ctx.exit(). Exit, Abort, KeyboardInterrupt/EOFError, ClickException and EPIPE OSError are caught and turned into exit codes and messages. With standalone_mode=False, the return value is returned and exceptions propagate.

compatibility_rules.claim: Supported Python is >=3.10, and the package is typed (Typing :: Typed classifier, py.typed file in src/click).

The public API is whatever src/click/__init__.py re-exports using the `X as X` form. Names beginning with an underscore are private. Old names are kept as lazy module `__getattr__` shims that emit DeprecationWarning.

Deprecation practice: the message says 'is deprecated and will be removed in Click 9.0' (or 9.1 for __version__), uses DeprecationWarning with stacklevel=2, and names the replacement. The old name still resolves to the private implementation.
core.py also has a module-level __getattr__ shim for BaseCommand and MultiCommand.
Each deprecated alias must have a test in test_deprecations.py (parametrized case plus an AttributeError check for unknown names).
Warning policy: pytest runs with filterwarnings=error, and the docs build uses -W.
Typing policy: mypy runs in strict mode over src and tests/typing, and pyright runs with --verifytypes click.
The code uses `from __future__ import annotations`. ruff enforces isort with force-single-line imports and the `typing as t` alias.
Changes are recorded in CHANGES.md using {pr}/{issue} roles. Docstrings use `.. versionchanged::` / `.. versionadded::` directives.
User-facing strings go through the gettext `_()` function. The deprecated-parameter message in handle_parse_result is one example.

cards.summary: src/click/core.py holds Click's runtime model. Context carries per-invocation state: params, parameter sources, resources and cleanup. Command parses args and invokes the callback. Group, plus its CommandCollection subclass, dispatches to subcommands, including chain mode. Parameter, Option and Argument implement the value pipeline: parser value, then consume_value (env var, default_map, default, prompt), then type_cast_value, then process_value (required check, callback), then handle_parse_result. handle_parse_result also arbitrates when several params share one name. An internal UNSET sentinel is used throughout and is converted to None before the user sees it. ParameterSource is an IntEnum ordered from most to least explicit. Command.main wraps everything with exception-to-exit-code handling.

interfaces.name: ParameterSource
interfaces.behavior: IntEnum with members PROMPT, COMMANDLINE, ENVIRONMENT, DEFAULT_MAP, DEFAULT (enum.auto, so values 1..5). Lower means more explicit, so comparisons such as `source < ParameterSource.DEFAULT_MAP` mean 'explicitly provided'. handle_parse_result uses this ordering for deprecation warnings and for arbitration.
edge_cases: Ordering was changed in 8.3.3 (IntEnum, reordered)
interfaces.signature: class ParameterSource(enum.IntEnum)

interfaces.name: Context.__init__
interfaces.behavior: Builds a context for a command. Stores parent, command, info_name, params={}, args=[] and further settings. Key args: obj, auto_envvar_prefix, default_map, terminal_width, max_content_width, resilient_parsing, allow_extra_args, allow_interspersed_args, ignore_unknown_options, help_option_names, token_normalize_func, color, show_default. Several of these are None by default so they can be inherited from the parent or from the command (not re-read in full).
edge_cases: Settings default to None and are inherited from parent where applicable
interfaces.signature: def __init__(self, command: Command, parent: Context | None=None, info_name: str | None=None, obj: t.Any | None=None, auto_envvar_prefix: str | None=None, default_map: cabc.MutableMapping[str, t.Any] | None=None, terminal_width: int | None=None, max_content_width: int | None=None, resilient_parsing: bool=False, allow_extra_args: bool | None=None, allow_interspersed_args: bool | None=None, ignore_unknown_options: bool | None=None, help_option_names: list[str] | None=None, token_normalize_func: t.Callable[[str], str] | None=None, color: bool | None=None, show_default: bool | None=None) -> None

interfaces.name: Context.scope
interfaces.behavior: Context manager that pushes the context onto the thread-local stack. With cleanup=False the context is not closed on exit. make_context uses it for parsing.
edge_cases: cleanup=False skips close()
interfaces.signature: def scope(self, cleanup: bool=True) -> cabc.Generator[Context]

interfaces.name: Context.with_resource
interfaces.behavior: Enters the given context manager, registers its exit to run on ctx.close(), and returns the entered value.
interfaces.signature: def with_resource(self, context_manager: AbstractContextManager[V]) -> V

interfaces.name: Context.call_on_close
interfaces.behavior: Registers a callback to run when the context closes. Returns the callback, so it can be used as a decorator.
interfaces.signature: def call_on_close(self, f: t.Callable[..., t.Any]) -> t.Callable[..., t.Any]

interfaces.name: Context.lookup_default
interfaces.behavior: Looks up name in default_map. If call=True and the value is callable, it is called. Returns None if the name is absent.
edge_cases: Callable defaults are invoked when call=True
interfaces.signature: def lookup_default(self, name: str, call: bool=True) -> t.Any | None

interfaces.name: Context.find_object
interfaces.behavior: Walks up the parent chain and returns the first ctx.obj that is an instance of object_type, or None if there is none.
edge_cases: Returns None when absent
interfaces.signature: def find_object(self, object_type: type[V]) -> V | None

interfaces.name: Context.ensure_object
interfaces.behavior: Calls find_object. If it returns None, creates object_type(), stores it in ctx.obj and returns it.
interfaces.signature: def ensure_object(self, object_type: type[V]) -> V

interfaces.name: Context.fail
interfaces.behavior: Raises UsageError(message, ctx).
interfaces.signature: def fail(self, message: str) -> t.NoReturn

interfaces.name: Context.exit
interfaces.behavior: Raises Exit(code), default 0. Context.abort raises Abort.
interfaces.signature: def exit(self, code: int=0) -> t.NoReturn

interfaces.name: Context.invoke
interfaces.behavior: If the first argument is a Command, a sub-context is created. Every exposed param not in kwargs is filled from param.get_default (UNSET becomes None) and passed through type_cast_value. Then kwargs are recorded in ctx.params and the command's callback is called. If the first argument is a plain callable, it is called with the given args and kwargs. The call runs inside augment_usage_errors and the context.
edge_cases: A command without a callback raises TypeError
Defaults are type-cast but required is not enforced
interfaces.signature: def invoke(self, callback: Command | t.Callable[..., V], /, *args: t.Any, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Any | V

interfaces.name: Context.forward
interfaces.behavior: Like invoke, but first copies all of the current ctx.params into kwargs for keys not already given. Only accepts Command objects.
edge_cases: A non-Command argument raises TypeError
interfaces.signature: def forward(self, cmd: Command, /, *args: t.Any, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Any

interfaces.name: Context.get_parameter_source
interfaces.behavior: Returns the ParameterSource for a parameter name, or None if no source was recorded. Context.set_parameter_source sets it.
edge_cases: Returns None when unrecorded
interfaces.signature: def get_parameter_source(self, name: str) -> ParameterSource | None

interfaces.name: Command.make_context
interfaces.behavior: Copies context_settings into extra without overriding explicit keys. Builds self.context_class(self, info_name=..., parent=..., **extra). Then runs self.parse_args(ctx, args) inside ctx.scope(cleanup=False) and returns the context without invoking the callback.
edge_cases: Explicit **extra wins over context_settings
interfaces.signature: def make_context(self, info_name: str | None, args: list[str], parent: Context | None=None, **extra: t.Any) -> Context

interfaces.name: Command.parse_args
interfaces.behavior: Raises NoArgsIsHelpError if there are no args, no_args_is_help is set and parsing is not resilient. Builds the parser and parses. For each param in iter_params_for_processing (eager params first, then in the order they were given on the command line) it calls handle_parse_result. Afterwards UNSET in ctx.params is converted to None. Leftover args cause ctx.fail('Got unexpected extra argument(s) (...)') unless allow_extra_args or resilient_parsing is set. Finally it sets ctx.args.
edge_cases: resilient_parsing suppresses errors
UNSET is converted to None only after all params are processed
interfaces.signature: def parse_args(self, ctx: Context, args: list[str]) -> list[str]

interfaces.name: Command.invoke
interfaces.behavior: If the command is deprecated, echoes a red 'DeprecationWarning: The command ... is deprecated.' message to stderr. Then, if a callback exists, returns ctx.invoke(callback, **ctx.params). Returns None otherwise.
edge_cases: No callback means None is returned
interfaces.signature: def invoke(self, ctx: Context) -> t.Any

interfaces.name: Command.main
interfaces.behavior: Uses sys.argv[1:] when args is None, with Windows glob expansion when windows_expand_args is true. Otherwise uses list(args). Detects prog_name, handles shell completion via the _PROG_COMPLETE env var and exits early. Runs make_context and invoke inside the context. With standalone_mode=True it calls ctx.exit() and ends with sys.exit. Exit sets the exit code. Abort prints 'Aborted!' and exits 1. EOFError/KeyboardInterrupt also lead to 'Aborted!'. ClickException is shown via e.show with e.exit_code. OSError with errno EPIPE is silenced, anything else is re-raised. With standalone_mode=False it returns rv, or e.exit_code for Exit, and re-raises Abort and ClickException. EOFError/KeyboardInterrupt are re-raised as Abort. Command.__call__ is an alias.
edge_cases: Exit in non-standalone mode returns the exit code, which is ambiguous with a return value
Chained commands can return [None, ...]
interfaces.signature: def main(self, args: cabc.Sequence[str] | None=None, prog_name: str | None=None, complete_var: str | None=None, standalone_mode: bool=True, windows_expand_args: bool=True, **extra: t.Any) -> t.Any

interfaces.name: Group.add_command
interfaces.behavior: Registers cmd under name or cmd.name. Runs _check_nested_chain(register=True) and stores it in self.commands.
edge_cases: No name raises TypeError
interfaces.signature: def add_command(self, cmd: Command, name: str | None=None) -> None

interfaces.name: Group.command
interfaces.behavior: Decorator that creates a command via decorators.command and registers it with add_command. Works with or without parentheses. Uses command_class when cls is not passed.
edge_cases: A bare callable together with kwargs triggers an AssertionError
interfaces.signature: def command(self, *args: t.Any, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[t.Callable[..., t.Any]], Command] | Command

interfaces.name: Group.result_callback
interfaces.behavior: Decorator that registers a result callback. It is called with (result, **ctx.params) after the subcommand runs. In chain mode the result is a list. replace=True allows replacing an existing callback.
edge_cases: Not read in full; replace semantics inferred from the signature
interfaces.signature: def result_callback(self, replace: bool=False) -> t.Callable[[F], F]

interfaces.name: Group.invoke
interfaces.behavior: Without a subcommand: if invoke_without_command is set, runs the group callback and passes its return value to the result callback (an empty list in chain mode). Otherwise fails with 'Missing command.'. In non-chain mode it resolves the command, sets ctx.invoked_subcommand, runs the group callback, builds the sub-context and invokes it, then runs the result callback. In chain mode it sets invoked_subcommand to '*' (or None), runs the group callback, creates all sub-contexts (allow_extra_args=True, allow_interspersed_args=False) and then invokes them in order. The result callback receives the list of results.
edge_cases: Group callback runs before the subcommand context is made
Chain contexts are all built before any runs
interfaces.signature: def invoke(self, ctx: Context) -> t.Any

interfaces.name: Group.resolve_command
interfaces.behavior: Calls get_command(ctx, name of args[0]). If not found and token_normalize_func is set, retries with the normalized name. If still not found and parsing is not resilient: when the token looks like an option it re-runs self.parse_args(ctx, args) so that --help and similar are handled by the group. Then it raises NoSuchCommand with command-name possibilities. Returns (name, cmd, args[1:]). Under resilient_parsing it returns (None, None, rest).
edge_cases: Resilient parsing yields (None, None, ...)
interfaces.signature: def resolve_command(self, ctx: Context, args: list[str]) -> tuple[str | None, Command | None, list[str]]

interfaces.name: CommandCollection.get_command
interfaces.behavior: Checks the group's own commands first, then each of the sources in order. In chain mode it validates nested chains. list_commands returns the sorted union of names. add_source appends a Group to sources.
edge_cases: Source params and callbacks are not used
Own commands take precedence over sources
interfaces.signature: def get_command(self, ctx: Context, cmd_name: str) -> Command | None

interfaces.name: Parameter.consume_value
interfaces.behavior: Value precedence: parser opts (COMMANDLINE), then envvar via value_from_envvar (ENVIRONMENT), then ctx.default_map via lookup_default (DEFAULT_MAP, including explicit None keys). A str from the default map is split via type.split_envvar_value when nargs != 1. Then get_default (DEFAULT). Returns (value, source), where value may be UNSET.
edge_cases: An empty envvar string is treated as unset
A key explicitly present in default_map with a None value counts as set
interfaces.signature: def consume_value(self, ctx: Context, opts: cabc.Mapping[str, t.Any]) -> tuple[t.Any, ParameterSource]

interfaces.name: Parameter.type_cast_value
interfaces.behavior: None becomes () for multiple or nargs=-1, otherwise None passes through. nargs==1 or a composite type: calls self.type(value, param, ctx). nargs=-1: converts each item into a tuple. nargs>1: requires exactly nargs items and returns a tuple. multiple: wraps the above in a tuple over the items.
edge_cases: A non-iterable raises 'Value must be an iterable.'
A wrong item count raises 'Takes N values but M were given.'
interfaces.signature: def type_cast_value(self, ctx: Context, value: t.Any) -> t.Any

interfaces.name: Parameter.process_value
interfaces.behavior: UNSET becomes () for multiple or nargs=-1, otherwise it skips the cast. Otherwise calls type_cast_value. Then, if required and value_is_missing, raises MissingParameter. Then, if a callback is set, calls callback(ctx, param, value). UNSET is shown to the callback as None, and other UNSET params in ctx.params are temporarily masked as None.
edge_cases: The callback return value replaces the value
Option.process_value gives an unset non-required bool flag the value False, without type-casting (callback still called)
interfaces.signature: def process_value(self, ctx: Context, value: t.Any) -> t.Any

interfaces.name: Parameter.handle_parse_result
interfaces.behavior: Inside augment_usage_errors it calls consume_value, records the source, emits a deprecation warning to stderr if deprecated and explicitly set (source < DEFAULT_MAP), and calls process_value. In resilient_parsing mode, exceptions from process_value are swallowed and the value is reset to UNSET. When several params share a name, arbitration decides the winner: the more explicit source wins; on a tie the later one wins unless it would downgrade an explicit default. The winner writes ctx.params[name] if expose_value is true. Returns (value, args).
edge_cases: expose_value=False params are not stored in ctx.params
Losers restore the previous source
interfaces.signature: def handle_parse_result(self, ctx: Context, opts: cabc.Mapping[str, t.Any], args: list[str]) -> tuple[t.Any, list[str]]

interfaces.name: Option.__init__
interfaces.behavior: Declares an option. It handles prompt (prompt=True derives text from the name), confirmation_prompt, prompt_required, hide_input, is_flag, flag_value (default UNSET), multiple, count (default 0 if unset), allow_from_autoenv, type, help, hidden, show_choices, show_envvar, show_default and deprecated. Flag kind is inferred in _infer_flag_kind and the type in _pick_type. It ends with a _validate step that raises on illegal combinations.
edge_cases: prompt=True without a name raises TypeError
Setting flag_value implies is_flag
interfaces.signature: def __init__(self, param_decls: cabc.Sequence[str] | None=None, show_default: bool | str | None=None, prompt: bool | str=False, confirmation_prompt: bool | str=False, prompt_required: bool=True, hide_input: bool=False, is_flag: bool | None=None, flag_value: t.Any=UNSET, multiple: bool=False, count: bool=False, allow_from_autoenv: bool=True, type: types.ParamType[t.Any] | t.Any | None=None, help: str | None=None, hidden: bool=False, show_choices: bool=True, show_envvar: bool=False, deprecated: bool | str=False, **attrs: t.Any) -> None

interfaces.name: Option.consume_value
interfaces.behavior: Calls Parameter.consume_value. If the parser yields FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE, it prompts (source PROMPT) when prompt is set and parsing is not resilient. Otherwise it uses flag_activation_value with source COMMANDLINE. For multiple options it replaces FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE items with the activation value. If the value is unset (or from default/default_map) and prompt is set and (required or prompt_required), it prompts.
edge_cases: Prompting is skipped under resilient_parsing
interfaces.signature: def consume_value(self, ctx: Context, opts: cabc.Mapping[str, Parameter]) -> tuple[t.Any, ParameterSource]

interfaces.name: Argument.__init__
interfaces.behavior: Positional parameter. If required is None, it is True when there is no default and nargs > 0 (default nargs is 1), and False when a default is given. A multiple kwarg raises TypeError. Exactly one decl is allowed, and the name is lowercased with '-' replaced by '_'. The metavar is upper-case, wrapped in [] if optional, and gets '...' when nargs != 1.
edge_cases: Zero decls with expose_value=True raises TypeError
More than one decl raises TypeError
interfaces.signature: def __init__(self, param_decls: cabc.Sequence[str], required: bool | None=None, help: str | None=None, **attrs: t.Any) -> None

cards.error_conventions: Runtime user errors use the ClickException family. Context.fail raises UsageError. Missing values raise MissingParameter. Bad conversion or a wrong nargs count raises BadParameter. An unknown subcommand raises NoSuchCommand. Control flow uses Exit and Abort. NoArgsIsHelpError is raised when there are no args and no_args_is_help is set. Programmer errors (a bad param declaration, a missing callback, forward given a non-Command, a missing command name) raise TypeError with plain messages. Messages are wrapped in gettext `_()` / ngettext, with sentences ending in a period, such as 'Value must be an iterable.' and 'Takes {nargs} values but {len} were given.'. Some messages are not terminated, such as 'Got unexpected extra argument (x)'. Deprecation is reported as red text on stderr, 'DeprecationWarning: The ... is deprecated.', and does not use warnings.warn.

cards.summary: src/click/decorators.py (626 lines) holds the decorator layer. It has context-passing decorators (pass_context, pass_obj, make_pass_decorator, pass_meta_key). It has command/group factories, which turn a function into a Command or Group. It has the param-attaching decorators option and argument. It has preconfigured eager or flag options: confirmation_option, password_option, version_option, custom_version_option and help_option. Params are stashed on `f.__click_params__` until command() consumes them in reversed order, which gives top-to-bottom declaration order. Preconfigured options use kwargs.setdefault, so callers can override most defaults. version_option and custom_version_option force their own callback.

interfaces.name: pass_context
interfaces.behavior: Wraps f so that get_current_context() is passed as first positional arg; uses update_wrapper. Does not use ctx.invoke.
edge_cases: Outside a context, get_current_context() raises RuntimeError at call time, not decoration time
interfaces.signature: def pass_context(f: t.Callable[te.Concatenate[Context, P], R]) -> t.Callable[P, R]

interfaces.name: pass_obj
interfaces.behavior: Wraps f, passing get_current_context().obj as first arg; update_wrapper preserves metadata.
edge_cases: Passes None if ctx.obj was never set
Does not use ctx.invoke
interfaces.signature: def pass_obj(f: t.Callable[te.Concatenate[T, P], R]) -> t.Callable[P, R]

interfaces.name: make_pass_decorator
interfaces.behavior: Returns a decorator factory. Wrapper gets the current context, then ctx.ensure_object(object_type) if ensure=True, else ctx.find_object(object_type) (innermost matching ctx.obj walking parents). Calls ctx.invoke(f, obj, *args, **kwargs).
edge_cases: ensure=False and no object found: obj is None, raises RuntimeError
ensure=True creates object_type() and stores it on ctx.obj
interfaces.signature: def make_pass_decorator(object_type: type[T], ensure: bool=False) -> t.Callable[[t.Callable[te.Concatenate[T, P], R]], t.Callable[P, R]]

interfaces.name: pass_meta_key
interfaces.behavior: Returns a decorator that passes ctx.meta[key] as first arg via ctx.invoke. The decorator's __doc__ is generated from doc_description, defaulting to "the 'key' key from :attr:`click.Context.meta`". doc_description is keyword-only. Added in 8.0.
edge_cases: Missing key raises KeyError at call time (direct dict index)
interfaces.signature: def pass_meta_key(key: str, *, doc_description: str | None=None) -> t.Callable[[t.Callable[te.Concatenate[T, P], R]], t.Callable[P, R]]

interfaces.name: command
interfaces.behavior: Creates a Command (or cls) from a function. Four typing overloads cover bare use (@command), name plus cls, cls only as keyword, and name only. If name is callable it is treated as the function, and asserts that cls is None and attrs is empty. Name defaults to f.__name__.lower() with _ replaced by -, then one trailing suffix (command, cmd, group, grp) stripped. Pops params from attrs (a given list is mutated in place) and extends it with reversed(f.__click_params__), then deletes that attribute. help defaults to f.__doc__ when attrs['help'] is None. Instantiates cls(name=..., callback=f, params=params, **attrs) and sets cmd.__doc__ = f.__doc__.
edge_cases: Applying to an existing Command raises TypeError
Bare use with cls or kwargs fails an assert, not a TypeError
Suffix stripping only happens on the derived name, not an explicit name
A function named only 'command' is not stripped, because rpartition gives no separator
attrs.pop('params') on the shared attrs dict means reusing one decorator object on a second function loses the explicit params
interfaces.signature: def command(name: str | _AnyCallable | None=None, cls: type[CmdType] | None=None, **attrs: t.Any) -> Command | t.Callable[[_AnyCallable], Command | CmdType]

interfaces.name: group
interfaces.behavior: Same as command with cls defaulting to Group. If name is callable it calls command(cls=cls, **attrs)(name); otherwise command(name, cls, **attrs).
edge_cases: Bare use with extra attrs is impossible because the callable is the name
interfaces.signature: def group(name: str | _AnyCallable | None=None, cls: type[GrpType] | None=None, **attrs: t.Any) -> Group | t.Callable[[_AnyCallable], Group | GrpType]

interfaces.name: argument
interfaces.behavior: Returns a decorator that builds cls(param_decls, **attrs), with cls defaulting to Argument. It attaches the param via _param_memo and returns f unchanged.
edge_cases: If f is already a Command the param is appended to f.params (at end, not reversed)
The Argument is built when the decorator is applied, not when argument() is called
interfaces.signature: def argument(*param_decls: str, cls: type[Argument] | None=None, **attrs: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[FC], FC]

interfaces.name: option
interfaces.behavior: Same as argument but builds an Option (cls defaults to Option). Stacked option decorators append to f.__click_params__ bottom-up, and command() reverses the list so the top decorator comes first.
edge_cases: Applied over an existing Command it appends directly to cmd.params
Each application creates a new Option instance
interfaces.signature: def option(*param_decls: str, cls: type[Option] | None=None, **attrs: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[FC], FC]

interfaces.name: confirmation_option
interfaces.behavior: Wraps option(). Default decl is --yes. Uses setdefault for is_flag=True, callback (ctx.abort() if value is falsy), expose_value=False, prompt=_('Do you want to continue?') and help=_('Confirm the action without prompting.').
edge_cases: Any default can be overridden through kwargs
Declining the prompt calls ctx.abort(), which raises Abort
interfaces.signature: def confirmation_option(*param_decls: str, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[FC], FC]

interfaces.name: password_option
interfaces.behavior: Wraps option(). Default decl is --password. Uses setdefault for prompt=True, confirmation_prompt=True and hide_input=True. The value is exposed to the function.
edge_cases: Overridable through kwargs
interfaces.signature: def password_option(*param_decls: str, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[FC], FC]

interfaces.name: version_option
interfaces.behavior: Eager --version flag with expose_value=False. If version and package_name are both None, it inspects the caller's frame globals for __name__ (using __package__ if '__main__') and takes the top-level segment as package_name. The callback is forced, so a user-supplied callback is overwritten. The callback returns early if the value is falsy or ctx.resilient_parsing is set. prog_name defaults to ctx.find_root().info_name. The version is resolved lazily at invocation via importlib.metadata.version(package_name). If that fails it tries packages_distributions() for a unique distribution. Output is message % {prog, package, version} through echo(color=ctx.color), then ctx.exit(). Default message is _('%(prog)s, version %(version)s'). The signature is version, *param_decls, then keyword-only package_name, prog_name and message.
edge_cases: Several distributions for one import name raise RuntimeError telling the user to pass package_name
Zero matches raise RuntimeError saying the package is not installed
version still None raises RuntimeError saying it could not be determined
Decl default is --version
The docstring says the message slots are frozen
interfaces.signature: def version_option(version: str | None=None, *param_decls: str, package_name: str | None=None, prog_name: str | None=None, message: str | None=None, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[FC], FC]

interfaces.name: custom_version_option
interfaces.behavior: Added in 8.5.0. Eager --version flag. Takes callback(ctx) -> str, whose return value is echoed (color=ctx.color) before ctx.exit(). The internal show_version callback is forced over any kwargs callback. It is a no-op when the value is falsy or ctx.resilient_parsing is set. Defaults are setdefault is_flag=True, expose_value=False, is_eager=True and help=_('Show the version and exit.'). Default decl is --version.
edge_cases: The callback return value is not type-checked; a non-str goes straight to echo
Any exception from the callback propagates
interfaces.signature: def custom_version_option(callback: t.Callable[[Context], str], *param_decls: str, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[FC], FC]

interfaces.name: help_option
interfaces.behavior: Eager --help flag. Callback show_help echoes ctx.get_help() (color=ctx.color) and calls ctx.exit(), unless the value is falsy or ctx.resilient_parsing is set. Defaults via setdefault are is_flag=True, expose_value=False, is_eager=True, help=_('Show this message and exit.') and callback=show_help. Default decl is --help.
edge_cases: A custom callback in kwargs replaces show_help
Names are customizable (see test_help_option_custom_names_and_class)
interfaces.signature: def help_option(*param_decls: str, **kwargs: t.Any) -> t.Callable[[FC], FC]

interfaces.name: _param_memo
interfaces.behavior: Private. Appends param to f.params if f is a Command. Otherwise it creates f.__click_params__ = [] if missing and appends. This is the point where decorators and command() communicate.
edge_cases: Sets an attribute on f, so it fails on objects that reject attributes, such as builtins or slotted callables
interfaces.signature: def _param_memo(f: t.Callable[..., t.Any], param: Parameter) -> None

cards.error_conventions: TypeError is raised when a callback is converted to a command twice (command, line 219). AssertionError (bare `assert` with a message) is used for misuse of the bare-decorator form (lines 211-212). RuntimeError is used for runtime resolution failures: no context object in make_pass_decorator, and version detection in version_option. Messages are lowercase-style sentences, quote names with !r, and end with a hint such as "Pass 'package_name' to disambiguate." or "Try passing 'package_name' instead." User-facing default strings are wrapped in gettext `_()`. Aborting goes through ctx.abort(), and early exit through ctx.exit(). Neither is raised directly here.

gaps.description: No decorator for a --verbose/-v counter or a --quiet/--debug flag, which are common canned options
gaps.why_plausible: Every canned option here is a thin setdefault wrapper around option(); a counting verbosity option would be the same size.

gaps.description: pass_context and pass_obj do not use ctx.invoke, while make_pass_decorator and pass_meta_key do. pass_meta_key has no ensure/default behavior.
gaps.why_plausible: A default or ensure parameter on pass_meta_key would mirror make_pass_decorator(ensure=True).

gaps.description: command() raises a bare AssertionError for misuse of the bare form, and the name of a Command object cannot be set from a decorator when it is applied twice
gaps.why_plausible: Converting the asserts to TypeError, matching the double-conversion check, would be a small consistency fix.

gaps.description: custom_version_option and version_option force their callback (kwargs['callback'] is overwritten), unlike help_option and confirmation_option, which use setdefault
gaps.why_plausible: The inconsistency means a user-supplied callback is silently ignored.

limitations: Params are stored on the function as __click_params__, and the order depends on command() reversing that list.
The command() decorator pops params from the shared attrs dict, so the decorator is not safely reusable.
version_option's package detection uses frame inspection, which is brittle in wrappers, and the version is only resolved when the option is invoked.
pass_context and pass_obj do not preserve the typed Context subclass beyond annotations.
argument() and option() accept **attrs untyped, so all validation happens in the Option/Argument constructors.
I did not read the typing tests or test_options.py contents in detail.

cards.summary: src/click/types.py defines ParamType (generic ABC: convert/fail/get_metavar/shell_complete/to_info_dict/split_envvar_value) and concrete types: FuncParamType, UNPROCESSED, STRING, Choice, DateTime, INT/IntRange, FLOAT/FloatRange, BOOL, UUID, File, Path, Tuple (composite). convert_type maps Python types/defaults/ParamType instances to ParamType singletons. Singletons are module-level t.Final instances at the end of the file. Failures go through ParamType.fail -> BadParameter.

interfaces.name: ParamType
interfaces.behavior: Generic ABC (line 65), class attrs is_composite=False, arity=1, name (must be set by subclass), envvar_list_splitter=None (whitespace). __call__ returns None for None, else self.convert(value,param,ctx). Base convert returns value unchanged. get_metavar and get_missing_message return None by default; shell_complete returns []. split_envvar_value does (rv or '').split(envvar_list_splitter). On Python<3.13 __class_getitem__ fills the 2nd type param with Any.
edge_cases: to_info_dict derives param_type from class name stripped of 'ParamType'/'ParameterType' suffix; falls back to that when subclass has no `name`
convert must tolerate param=None and ctx=None (prompts)
split_envvar_value on None-like falsy rv gives [] when splitter is None, [''] otherwise
interfaces.signature: class ParamType(t.Generic[_ValueT_co, _InputT_contra], abc.ABC)

interfaces.behavior: Choice(choices, case_sensitive=True); choices stored as tuple (iterable consumed once). convert normalizes value via normalize_choice, builds {original: normalized} mapping each call, returns first original whose normalized equals. Enum members normalize to .name, others to str(). normalize_choice applies ctx.token_normalize_func then casefold if not case_sensitive. get_metavar: for options with show_choices False uses upper-cased type names of choices; else 'a|b|c'; wrapped in {} for required argument, [] otherwise. shell_complete prefix matches normalized choices.

duplicate normalized values: first match wins (no check despite docstring)

cards.error_conventions: Validation failures call ParamType.fail which raises click.exceptions.BadParameter(message, ctx, param). Messages are gettext-wrapped (_ / ngettext), use {value!r} reprs, end with a period (e.g. "'d' is not one of 'a', 'b'."; "{value!r} is not a valid integer."; "{name} {filename!r} does not exist."). Programmer errors use TypeError (FloatRange open+clamp), RuntimeError (open float clamp), AssertionError (uninstantiated ParamType class in convert_type). Non-ValueError exceptions from conversion propagate.

cards.summary: src/click/parser.py is Click's private argv parser, adapted from optparse. Core.Command.make_parser (core.py:1227) builds an _OptionParser(ctx), and each Parameter's add_to_parser registers itself. Command.parse_args (core.py:1371-1372) then calls parser.parse_args. The parser does no type conversion or defaults. It returns raw values in a dict keyed by dest, the leftover args, and a list of parameter objects in command-line order. Unset values are the UNSET sentinel, and FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE marks an option whose value was omitted. The old public names (OptionParser, Argument, Option, split_opt, normalize_opt, ParsingState, split_arg_string) are served by a module `__getattr__` that emits DeprecationWarning.

interfaces.name: _OptionParser
interfaces.behavior: Internal parser class. __init__(ctx=None) stores ctx and defaults allow_interspersed_args=True and ignore_unknown_options=False. If ctx is given, both flags are copied from ctx. It starts with _opt_prefixes={'-','--'}, plus empty _short_opt, _long_opt and _args. The docstring carries a '.. deprecated:: 8.2' note.
edge_cases: ctx=None disables token normalization and resilient parsing
Flags are copied once at construction, so later changes to ctx are not seen
interfaces.signature: class _OptionParser  # __init__(self, ctx: Context | None=None)

interfaces.name: _OptionParser.add_option
interfaces.behavior: Normalizes each opt string with _normalize_opt (which applies ctx.token_normalize_func). It builds an _Option, adds its prefixes to _opt_prefixes, and registers its short opts in _short_opt and its long opts in _long_opt. The dest is passed in explicitly and never inferred. action defaults to 'store' and nargs to 1. Valid actions are store, store_const, append, append_const and count.
edge_cases: An opt with no prefix (starts alnum) raises ValueError from _Option
An unknown action is not checked here; it fails later in _Option.process
Re-registering an opt string silently overwrites the earlier one
interfaces.signature: def add_option(self, obj: CoreOption, opts: cabc.Sequence[str], dest: str | None, action: str | None=None, nargs: int=1, const: t.Any | None=None) -> None

interfaces.name: _OptionParser.add_argument
interfaces.behavior: Appends an _Argument(obj, dest, nargs) to _args. Positional order is the order of calls.
edge_cases: Two arguments with nargs<0 cause a TypeError later, in _unpack_args
interfaces.signature: def add_argument(self, obj: CoreArgument, dest: str | None, nargs: int=1) -> None

interfaces.name: _OptionParser.parse_args
interfaces.behavior: Builds a _ParsingState(args), runs _process_args_for_options and then _process_args_for_args. It returns (state.opts, state.largs, state.order). The input list is consumed (popped) in place.
edge_cases: UsageError is swallowed when ctx.resilient_parsing is true, and the partial results are returned
With ctx=None the error always propagates
interfaces.signature: def parse_args(self, args: list[str]) -> tuple[dict[str, t.Any], list[str], list[CoreParameter]]

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._process_args_for_options
interfaces.behavior: Pops from rargs one arg at a time. A bare '--' stops processing and is dropped. An arg whose first character is in _opt_prefixes and whose length is >1 goes to _process_opts. Any other arg is appended to largs if interspersed args are allowed. Otherwise it is pushed back onto rargs and parsing stops.
edge_cases: A lone '-' is treated as positional
The '--' check uses `return`, so the remaining args stay in rargs
interfaces.signature: def _process_args_for_options(self, state: _ParsingState) -> None

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._process_args_for_args
interfaces.behavior: Calls _unpack_args(largs+rargs, [nargs of each arg]) and then each _Argument.process. The leftovers become largs and rargs is cleared.
edge_cases: Extra positionals are returned as leftover args
Missing positionals are UNSET
interfaces.signature: def _process_args_for_args(self, state: _ParsingState) -> None

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._process_opts
interfaces.behavior: Splits the arg on the first '=' to get an explicit value and normalizes the name. It tries _match_long_opt first, so single-dash long options like -foo match. On NoSuchOption it falls back to _match_short_opt if the arg's first two characters are not a registered prefix. For a '--x' arg it re-raises, unless ignore_unknown_options is set, in which case it appends the arg to largs.
edge_cases: An explicit '=value' on a short option is treated as part of the arg string
interfaces.signature: def _process_opts(self, arg: str, state: _ParsingState) -> None

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._match_long_opt
interfaces.behavior: Looks the name up in _long_opt. A value-taking option has the explicit value inserted at rargs[0] and then reads its value through _get_value_from_state. A flag with an explicit value raises BadOptionUsage; otherwise its value is UNSET. It finishes with option.process.
edge_cases: Unknown opt raises NoSuchOption with possibilities=_long_opt for suggestions
interfaces.signature: def _match_long_opt(self, opt: str, explicit_value: str | None, state: _ParsingState) -> None

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._match_short_opt
interfaces.behavior: Walks the characters of a clustered arg such as -abc. A value-taking option consumes the rest of the arg as its value. With ignore_unknown_options, unknown characters are collected and re-appended to largs as prefix+chars.
edge_cases: Each char is normalized individually
The prefix is arg[0]
interfaces.signature: def _match_short_opt(self, arg: str, state: _ParsingState) -> None

interfaces.name: _OptionParser._get_value_from_state
interfaces.behavior: Takes nargs values from rargs. If fewer than nargs remain, it returns FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE when obj._flag_needs_value is set, and otherwise raises BadOptionUsage. For nargs==1, if the option allows an omitted value and the next arg looks like an option, it returns FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE instead of consuming it. For nargs>1 it returns a tuple.
edge_cases: The message is pluralized with ngettext
interfaces.signature: def _get_value_from_state(self, option_name: str, option: _Option, state: _ParsingState) -> str | cabc.Sequence[str] | T_UNSET | T_FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE

interfaces.name: _Option
interfaces.behavior: Holds obj, dest, action, nargs, const, prefixes, _short_opts and _long_opts. An opt is short if it has a 1-character prefix and a 1-character name; everything else is long. takes_value is true for the store and append actions. process(value, state) applies the action to state.opts and appends obj to state.order.
edge_cases: An opt with no prefix raises ValueError 'Invalid start character for option (x)'
An unknown action raises ValueError("unknown action '...'") at process time
count adds 1 starting from 0
append and append_const use setdefault(dest, [])
interfaces.signature: class _Option  # __init__(self, obj: CoreOption, opts: cabc.Sequence[str], dest: str | None, action: str | None=None, nargs: int=1, const: t.Any | None=None)

interfaces.name: _Argument
interfaces.behavior: Holds dest, nargs and obj. process(value, state) sets state.opts[dest]=value and appends obj to state.order. For nargs>1, a partial tuple (some UNSET) raises BadArgumentUsage, and an all-UNSET tuple becomes UNSET. An empty tuple (from nargs=-1 with nothing left) becomes UNSET.
edge_cases: Partial nargs>1 values raise
Empty variadic values are UNSET, not ()
interfaces.signature: class _Argument  # __init__(self, obj: CoreArgument, dest: str | None, nargs: int=1)

interfaces.name: _ParsingState
interfaces.behavior: Mutable state with opts (dict), largs (list), rargs (the input list) and order (list of params).
interfaces.signature: class _ParsingState  # __init__(self, rargs: list[str])

interfaces.name: _unpack_args
interfaces.behavior: Distributes args across nargs_spec. A positive nargs takes that many, with UNSET fill for missing items (a tuple when nargs>1). A negative nargs takes all the remainder, and specs after it are filled from the right. It returns (tuple of values, leftover list).
edge_cases: Missing items are UNSET
The wildcard slot is a tuple, possibly empty
interfaces.signature: def _unpack_args(args: cabc.Sequence[str], nargs_spec: cabc.Sequence[int]) -> tuple[cabc.Sequence[str | cabc.Sequence[str | T_UNSET] | T_UNSET], list[str]]

interfaces.name: _split_opt
interfaces.behavior: Returns (prefix, rest). An alnum first character gives ('', opt). A doubled first character gives (opt[:2], opt[2:]). Otherwise it returns (first, opt[1:]).
edge_cases: An empty string yields first='' and ('', '')
interfaces.signature: def _split_opt(opt: str) -> tuple[str, str]

interfaces.name: _normalize_opt
interfaces.behavior: Applies ctx.token_normalize_func to the name part and keeps the prefix. It returns opt unchanged if ctx is None or no func is set.
edge_cases: ctx=None returns opt unchanged
interfaces.signature: def _normalize_opt(opt: str, ctx: Context | None) -> str

interfaces.name: __getattr__
interfaces.behavior: Module-level shim. For OptionParser, Argument, Option, split_opt, normalize_opt and ParsingState, it emits a DeprecationWarning (stacklevel=2) and returns globals()['_'+name]. split_arg_string is lazily imported from click.shell_completion with its own warning.
edge_cases: Unknown names raise AttributeError(name)
interfaces.signature: def __getattr__(name: str) -> object

cards.error_conventions: Usage problems raise click.exceptions subclasses. NoSuchOption is raised for unknown options and is given possibilities for suggestions. BadOptionUsage(option_name, msg) covers a missing value or a value attached to a flag. BadArgumentUsage covers a partial nargs on an argument. Messages are gettext-wrapped and formatted with {name!r}, for example "Option '--x' requires an argument." and "Option {name!r} requires {nargs} arguments." (pluralized with ngettext). Programmer errors use ValueError (invalid option prefix, unknown action) and TypeError (two variadic arguments). The module `__getattr__` raises AttributeError for unknown names and warns with DeprecationWarning.

examples.description: Default prefixes of a fresh parser
examples.code:
parser = _OptionParser()
assert parser._opt_prefixes == {"-", "--"}

examples.description: Custom prefixes are collected through Option.add_to_parser
examples.code:
ctx = click.Context(click.Command("test"))
parser = _OptionParser(ctx)
click.Option("+p", is_flag=True).add_to_parser(parser, ctx)
click.Option("!e", is_flag=True).add_to_parser(parser, ctx)
assert parser._opt_prefixes == {"-", "--", "+", "!"}

examples.description: Deprecated attribute access must be wrapped in pytest.warns
examples.code:
with pytest.warns(DeprecationWarning, match=name):
    value = getattr(module, name)
assert value == target

tests.how_it_asserts: Plain functions with bare asserts. They check the _opt_prefixes set on _OptionParser directly, with and without custom-prefix options added via Option.add_to_parser. Parsing behavior itself is mostly covered indirectly by tests/test_options.py and tests/test_arguments.py (not read here).

test_attr_deprecated is parametrized over (module, name, target). It uses pytest.warns(DeprecationWarning, match=name) around getattr and asserts equality with the _-prefixed target. test_unknown_attribute_raises expects AttributeError for click, click.core, click.parser and click.utils.

extension_points.name: Parameter.add_to_parser
extension_points.what_could_attach: The abstract hook (core.py:2516) that each Parameter subclass implements to register itself with the parser. Option's version is at core.py:3325 and Argument's at core.py:3800. A custom Parameter can call parser.add_option or add_argument with its own action and const.

extension_points.name: Command.make_parser
extension_points.what_could_attach: Subclasses can override it to return a customized _OptionParser subclass or to add extra options.

extension_points.name: _Option.process
extension_points.what_could_attach: The action dispatch if/elif chain. A new action such as 'extend' or 'store_true_once' would be added here, with takes_value updated to match.

extension_points.name: _OptionParser._opt_prefixes
extension_points.what_could_attach: The set of recognized option prefixes. It is extended automatically when options with new prefixes are added.

extension_points.name: _normalize_opt
extension_points.what_could_attach: Hooks into Context.token_normalize_func, for example for case-insensitive or alias normalization of option names.

gaps.description: Unknown-action validation at add_option time, so a bad action fails when registered rather than at parse time
gaps.why_plausible: _Option.__init__ already validates prefixes eagerly, but the action is only checked in process() (parser.py:181).

gaps.description: Detection of duplicate or conflicting option registrations
gaps.why_plausible: add_option silently overwrites entries in _short_opt and _long_opt (parser.py:285-288).

gaps.description: Unique-prefix abbreviation matching of long options (as argparse does)
gaps.why_plausible: _match_long_opt requires an exact match and only offers 'possibilities' for suggestions (parser.py:366-367).

gaps.description: Explicit '=value' support for short options, such as -o=value
gaps.why_plausible: The '=' split in _process_opts feeds only the long-option path. Short options fall back to _match_short_opt with the '=' as part of the value.

gaps.description: Direct unit tests of parse_args, _unpack_args and the error paths
gaps.why_plausible: tests/test_parser.py covers only the prefix sets, so direct parser-level tests are thin.

limitations: The module is private and deprecated; the docstring says it will be removed in Click 9.0, and the shim message points users to the stdlib optparse.
There is no type conversion or defaulting; everything is raw strings, UNSET or FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE.
Flags are copied from ctx once, in __init__.
Actions are plain strings dispatched through an if/elif chain.
No abbreviation matching of long options.
In resilient_parsing mode, UsageError is swallowed and partial results are returned.
I did not read tests/test_options.py, tests/test_arguments.py or tests/test_basic.py, which exercise the parser indirectly.

cards.summary: termui.py is the public front-end for interactive terminal helpers. prompt/confirm loop over a module-level input function (visible_prompt_func = input, or hidden_prompt_func = getpass). style/unstyle/secho build and strip ANSI codes. progressbar, edit, launch, getchar, raw_terminal and get_pager_file lazily import their implementations from _termui_impl. echo_via_pager, clear and pause are implemented here, on top of get_pager_file, echo, getchar and isatty.

interfaces.name: prompt
interfaces.behavior: Prompts until valid input (termui.py:168-286). value_proc defaults to convert_type(type, default). Prompt text comes from _build_prompt: it appends Choice choices if show_choices, and ' [default]' if show_default is true and default is not None. A str show_default is shown instead of the default. Empty input returns the default if default is not None, otherwise it re-prompts. The default goes through value_proc like typed input. Uses hidden_prompt_func if hide_input, else visible_prompt_func, via _readline_prompt. confirmation_prompt=True uses 'Repeat for confirmation'; a str customizes it. A mismatch echoes 'Error: The two entered values do not match.' and restarts. A UsageError from value_proc is echoed as 'Error: {message}', and the message is masked with '***' if hide_input. KeyboardInterrupt and EOFError become Abort, with an extra newline echoed if hide_input.
edge_cases: default=None with empty input loops forever until input or abort
empty first value and empty confirmation value are treated as matching
a non-str default is cast to str only for typing; it still goes through value_proc
err=True redirects stdout to stderr during input()
interfaces.signature: def prompt(text: str, default: V | str | None=None, hide_input: bool=False, confirmation_prompt: bool | str=False, type: ParamType[V, str] | type[V] | None=None, value_proc: t.Callable[[str], V] | None=None, prompt_suffix: str=': ', show_default: bool | str=True, err: bool=False, show_choices: bool=True) -> V

interfaces.name: confirm
interfaces.behavior: Yes/no prompt (289-345). Accepts y/yes/n/no, case-insensitive and stripped. Empty input returns default unless default is None. Anything else echoes 'Error: invalid input' and repeats. The suffix shows y/n, Y/n or y/N via _build_prompt. abort=True raises Abort on a negative answer. KeyboardInterrupt and EOFError become Abort.
edge_cases: default=None requires an explicit answer
show_default=False hides the [Y/n] hint
interfaces.signature: def confirm(text: str, default: bool | None=False, abort: bool=False, prompt_suffix: str=': ', show_default: bool=True, err: bool=False) -> bool

interfaces.name: get_pager_file
interfaces.behavior: Returns a context manager yielding a writable text file for pager output (348-364). Resolves color via resolve_color_default, then delegates to _termui_impl.get_pager_file(color=...). Added in 8.4.0.
edge_cases: color=None means autodetect
interfaces.signature: def get_pager_file(color: bool | None=None) -> t.ContextManager[t.TextIO]

interfaces.name: echo_via_pager
interfaces.behavior: Pages text (367-399). Accepts a str, an iterable, or a generator function; a generator function is called. Non-str elements are converted with str(). Writes each element to get_pager_file and flushes after every write, then writes a trailing newline (chained '\n').
edge_cases: a plain str becomes a one-element list
a generator object (not a function) is handled as a general iterable
interfaces.signature: def echo_via_pager(text_or_generator: cabc.Iterable[str] | t.Callable[[], cabc.Iterable[str]] | str, color: bool | None=None) -> None

interfaces.name: progressbar
interfaces.behavior: Builds a _termui_impl.ProgressBar (443-599) after resolving color. Defaults: show_eta=True, fill_char '#', empty_char '-', bar_template '%(label)s  [%(bar)s]  %(info)s', info_sep two spaces, width 36 (0 means full terminal width), update_min_steps=1. The length-only overload has no iterable or item_show_func. hidden=True suppresses all output; with no tty and hidden=False, only the label is printed.
edge_cases: neither iterable nor length is rejected by ProgressBar (see test_progressbar_init_exceptions)
show_percent defaults to True only if a length is known
interfaces.signature: def progressbar(iterable: cabc.Iterable[V] | None=None, length: int | None=None, label: str | None=None, hidden: bool=False, show_eta: bool=True, show_percent: bool | None=None, show_pos: bool=False, item_show_func: t.Callable[[V | None], str | None] | None=None, fill_char: str='#', empty_char: str='-', bar_template: str='%(label)s  [%(bar)s]  %(info)s', info_sep: str='  ', width: int=36, file: t.TextIO | None=None, color: bool | None=None, update_min_steps: int=1) -> ProgressBar[V]

interfaces.name: clear
interfaces.behavior: Clears the screen (602-613). Does nothing if stdout is not a tty. Otherwise echoes '\033[2J\033[1;1H' with nl=False.
edge_cases: no-op when piped
interfaces.signature: def clear() -> None

interfaces.name: style
interfaces.behavior: Returns text wrapped in ANSI codes (641-765). A non-str text is converted with str(). Codes are emitted in a fixed order: fg, bg (offset 10), bold, dim, underline, overline, italic, blink, reverse, strikethrough. A flag set to None emits nothing; False emits the off code (22 for bold and dim, 24, 55, 23, 25, 27, 29). reset=True appends \033[0m. Colors can be a name, an int 0-255, or an RGB 3-tuple/list.
edge_cases: True/False are rejected as colors
index 0 is valid as of 8.5.0
unknown name, out-of-range int or bad tuple raises ValueError
interfaces.signature: def style(text: t.Any, fg: int | tuple[int, int, int] | str | None=None, bg: int | tuple[int, int, int] | str | None=None, bold: bool | None=None, dim: bool | None=None, underline: bool | None=None, overline: bool | None=None, italic: bool | None=None, blink: bool | None=None, reverse: bool | None=None, strikethrough: bool | None=None, reset: bool=True) -> str

interfaces.name: unstyle
interfaces.behavior: Strips ANSI codes from text by delegating to _compat.strip_ansi (768-777).
interfaces.signature: def unstyle(text: str) -> str

interfaces.name: secho
interfaces.behavior: echo(style(message, **styles), file, nl, err, color) (780-811). A None message is passed straight to echo. bytes and bytearray messages skip styling.
edge_cases: message=None prints only a newline, or nothing with nl=False
unknown style kwargs raise TypeError from style()
interfaces.signature: def secho(message: t.Any | None=None, file: t.IO[t.AnyStr] | None=None, nl: bool=True, err: bool=False, color: bool | None=None, **styles: t.Any) -> None

interfaces.name: edit
interfaces.behavior: Opens an editor (848-920). It builds _termui_impl.Editor(editor, env, require_save, extension). With filename=None it returns ed.edit(text), which is None if the editor saved nothing and require_save is true. With filename (a str or PathLike is wrapped in a tuple) it calls ed.edit_files and returns None. The require_save default is False in the bytes overload and True otherwise.
edge_cases: when filename is given, require_save and extension are ignored
filename accepts an iterable of paths for editors that handle several files
interfaces.signature: def edit(text: str | bytes | bytearray | None=None, editor: str | None=None, env: cabc.Mapping[str, str] | None=None, require_save: bool=True, extension: str='.txt', filename: str | os.PathLike[str] | cabc.Iterable[str | os.PathLike[str]] | None=None) -> str | bytes | bytearray | None

interfaces.name: launch
interfaces.behavior: Calls _termui_impl.open_url(url, wait, locate) and returns the exit code (923-949). locate=True opens a file manager instead. wait=True only works if the launched program blocks.
edge_cases: xdg-open does not block
interfaces.signature: def launch(url: str, wait: bool=False, locate: bool=False) -> int

interfaces.name: getchar
interfaces.behavior: Reads one character (957-984). On first call it caches _termui_impl.getchar in the module global _getchar. If _getchar is already set it uses that, so tests can override it by setting click.termui._getchar. The echo flag shows the typed character.
edge_cases: may return more than one character
always reads from the terminal rather than piped stdin
interfaces.signature: def getchar(echo: bool=False) -> str

interfaces.name: raw_terminal
interfaces.behavior: Returns the _termui_impl.raw_terminal() context manager, which yields an int (987-990). It has no docstring and is not in the documented API.
interfaces.signature: def raw_terminal() -> AbstractContextManager[int]

interfaces.name: pause
interfaces.behavior: Waits for a keypress (993-1024). Returns immediately if stdin or stdout is not a tty. info defaults to 'Press any key to continue...'; an empty string prints nothing. Calls getchar(), swallowing KeyboardInterrupt and EOFError. A trailing newline is echoed in a finally block if info is truthy.
edge_cases: info='' suppresses the message and the newline
interfaces.signature: def pause(info: str | None=None, err: bool=False) -> None

interfaces.name: hidden_prompt_func
interfaces.behavior: Calls getpass.getpass(prompt) (79-82). It is a module-level hook used when hide_input is true.
interfaces.signature: def hidden_prompt_func(prompt: str) -> str

interfaces.name: visible_prompt_func
interfaces.behavior: Module-level hook, default builtin input (34). It is used by prompt and confirm, and tests monkeypatch it. It is looked up at call time.
interfaces.signature: visible_prompt_func: t.Callable[[str], str] = input

interfaces.name: _build_prompt
interfaces.behavior: Builds the prompt string (108-125): text, then the optional Choice list, then the default preview, then the suffix. A str show_default renders as ' [(str)]'. File defaults are rendered by their name via _format_default.
edge_cases: default None shows no preview unless show_default is a str
interfaces.signature: def _build_prompt(text: str, suffix: str, show_default: bool | str=False, default: object | None=None, show_choices: bool=True, type: object | None=None) -> str

interfaces.name: _interpret_color
interfaces.behavior: Converts a color to an SGR parameter string (616-638). Names map through the _ansi_colors dict. An int 0-255 becomes '38;5;N' (48 with offset 10). A 3-int tuple or list becomes '38;2;r;g;b'.

cards.summary: src/click/shell_completion.py implements Click's tab completion. shell_complete() parses the `<shell>_<instruction>` value of the env var. It looks up a ShellComplete subclass in the `_available_shells` registry and either prints the shell script (`source`) or prints completions (`complete`). Command._main_shell_completion (core.py:1619-1649) calls it and then calls sys.exit with its return value. ShellComplete.get_completions resolves a Context chain (`_resolve_context`), picks the object that should complete (`_resolve_incomplete`), and calls that object's `.shell_complete(ctx, incomplete)`. That returns a list of CompletionItem. Each shell subclass reads COMP_WORDS and COMP_CWORD from os.environ and formats items in its own wire format. Bash, Zsh, Fish and PowerShell are built in. Other shells can be added with add_completion_class.

interfaces.name: shell_complete
interfaces.behavior: Does `shell, _, instruction = instruction.partition('_')`, then looks up the class with get_completion_class(shell). It builds `comp_cls(cli, ctx_args, prog_name, complete_var)`. For 'source' it writes `comp.source().encode()` with echo(nl=False) and returns 0. For 'complete' it writes `comp.complete().encode()` with echo (newline appended) and returns 0. Output is written as bytes so Windows does not turn LF into CRLF.
edge_cases: Unknown shell returns 1
Unknown instruction returns 1
A value with no underscore gives shell=whole string and instruction='', so it returns 1 unless the shell name is unregistered, which also returns 1
interfaces.signature: def shell_complete(cli: Command, ctx_args: cabc.MutableMapping[str, t.Any], prog_name: str, complete_var: str, instruction: str) -> t.Literal[0, 1]

interfaces.name: CompletionItem
interfaces.behavior: Generic class with __slots__ ('value','type','help','_info'). `type` defaults to 'plain'. Click uses 'dir' and 'file' for special shell handling. `help` defaults to None. Extra kwargs go into `_info`.
edge_cases: __getattr__ returns None for any unknown attribute instead of raising AttributeError (`_info.get(name)`)
Extra kwargs are not used by built-in shells
interfaces.signature: class CompletionItem(t.Generic[_ValueT_co])  # __init__(self, value: _ValueT_co, type: str='plain', help: str | None=None, **kwargs: t.Any)

interfaces.name: CompletionItem.__init__
interfaces.behavior: Sets value, type, help and `_info=kwargs`.
edge_cases: Arbitrary kwargs accepted
interfaces.signature: def __init__(self, value: _ValueT_co, type: str='plain', help: str | None=None, **kwargs: t.Any) -> None

interfaces.name: CompletionItem.__getattr__
interfaces.behavior: Returns `self._info.get(name)`. It is only called when normal attribute lookup fails.
edge_cases: Missing keys give None
interfaces.signature: def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> t.Any

interfaces.name: ShellComplete
interfaces.behavior: Base class. Takes cli, ctx_args, prog_name and complete_var. Subclasses set the class attributes `name` and `source_template`, and implement get_completion_args and format_completion. complete() runs get_completion_args, then get_completions, then format_completion per item, and joins with '\n'.
edge_cases: The base class has no `name` or `source_template` defaults, so using it directly for source() fails
The tests use the base class directly for get_completions
interfaces.signature: class ShellComplete  # __init__(self, cli: Command, ctx_args: cabc.MutableMapping[str, t.Any], prog_name: str, complete_var: str)

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.func_name
interfaces.behavior: Property. Replaces '-' with '_' in prog_name, strips non-word ASCII characters, and returns `_{safe}_completion`.
edge_cases: Dots and other punctuation are removed (not turned into underscores)
interfaces.signature: def func_name(self) -> str

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.source_vars
interfaces.behavior: Returns a dict with complete_func, complete_var and prog_name for formatting the template.
edge_cases: Subclasses can override this to add template variables
interfaces.signature: def source_vars(self) -> _SourceVarsDict

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.source
interfaces.behavior: Returns `self.source_template % self.source_vars()`, a %-style format.
edge_cases: Literal % in a custom template must be escaped as %%
interfaces.signature: def source(self) -> str

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.get_completion_args
interfaces.behavior: Abstract. Returns (args, incomplete).
interfaces.signature: def get_completion_args(self) -> tuple[list[str], str]

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.get_completions
interfaces.behavior: Calls `_resolve_context(cli, ctx_args, prog_name, args)`, then `_resolve_incomplete(ctx, args, incomplete)`. Then returns `obj.shell_complete(ctx, incomplete)`.
edge_cases: incomplete may be ''
`args` can be mutated, because an `--opt=val` incomplete appends the option name to it
ctx_args gets resilient_parsing=True set on it (mutated)
interfaces.signature: def get_completions(self, args: list[str], incomplete: str) -> list[CompletionItem[str]]

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.format_completion
interfaces.behavior: Abstract. Turns a CompletionItem into a string for the shell script.
interfaces.signature: def format_completion(self, item: CompletionItem[str]) -> str

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.complete
interfaces.behavior: Returns the newline-joined formatted completions.
edge_cases: No completions gives an empty string
interfaces.signature: def complete(self) -> str

interfaces.name: BashComplete
interfaces.behavior: name='bash'. get_completion_args splits COMP_WORDS with split_arg_string and reads int(COMP_CWORD). args = cwords[1:cword]; incomplete = cwords[cword], or '' on IndexError. format_completion returns `type,value` and ignores help. source() first runs _check_version.
edge_cases: Missing env vars raise KeyError
A non-integer COMP_CWORD raises ValueError
Help text is dropped
interfaces.signature: class BashComplete(ShellComplete)

interfaces.name: BashComplete._check_version
interfaces.behavior: Static method. Runs `bash --norc -c 'echo ${BASH_VERSION}'` with subprocess. It echoes a message to stderr if bash is older than 4.4 or the version cannot be detected. It does not raise or abort.
edge_cases: No bash on PATH prints the 'Couldn't detect Bash version' message
Tests patch it out with monkeypatch
interfaces.signature: def _check_version() -> None

interfaces.name: ZshComplete
interfaces.behavior: name='zsh'. Same args logic as Bash. format_completion returns `type\nvalue\nhelp` with help defaulting to '_'. Colons in value are escaped as `\:` only when help is not '_'.
edge_cases: Colon escaping applies only to items that have help text
The script is deliberately frozen for backward compatibility
interfaces.signature: class ZshComplete(ShellComplete)

interfaces.name: FishComplete
interfaces.behavior: name='fish'. COMP_CWORD holds the partial word itself, not an index. args = cwords[1:]. If incomplete is non-empty it is passed through split_arg_string(...)[0], and the same word is popped from args if it is the last one. format_completion returns `type,value` and appends `\t<help>` when help is set. In help, newlines are escaped as `\n` and tabs become spaces (8.4.2).
edge_cases: An empty COMP_CWORD gives incomplete=''
A quoted partial word is unquoted by the split
interfaces.signature: class FishComplete(ShellComplete)

interfaces.name: PowerShellComplete
interfaces.behavior:
name='powershell' (added in 8.5.0). Same args logic as Bash, using an index COMP_CWORD. format_completion returns `type
value
help`, with help defaulting to '_'.  and 
 in help become spaces.
edge_cases: The PowerShell script consumes 3 lines per item
interfaces.signature: class PowerShellComplete(ShellComplete)

interfaces.name: add_completion_class
interfaces.behavior: Sets `_available_shells[name or cls.name] = cls` and returns cls, so it works as a decorator (no-argument form only).
edge_cases: Overwrites an existing registration silently
Raises AttributeError if name is None and cls has no `name`
interfaces.signature: def add_completion_class(cls: type[_ShellCompleteT], name: str | None=None) -> type[_ShellCompleteT]

interfaces.name: get_completion_class
interfaces.behavior: Returns `_available_shells.get(shell)`, or None if the shell is not registered. Typing overloads exist for bash, fish and zsh. There is no overload for powershell, which falls to the `str` overload.
edge_cases: Unknown shell returns None
interfaces.signature: def get_completion_class(shell: str) -> type[ShellComplete] | None

interfaces.name: split_arg_string
interfaces.behavior: Uses shlex.shlex(posix=True) with whitespace_split=True and commenters=''. If shlex raises ValueError (unclosed quote or trailing backslash), it appends the partial token `lex.token` to the output.
edge_cases: 'example \'my file' gives ['example','my file']
'example my\\' gives ['example','my']
Empty string gives []
'#' is not treated as a comment
interfaces.signature: def split_arg_string(string: str) -> list[str]

interfaces.name: _resolve_context
interfaces.behavior: Sets ctx_args['resilient_parsing']=True and calls cli.make_context(prog_name, args.copy(), **ctx_args). For Groups it follows subcommands with resolve_command and make_context(resilient_parsing=True). Chained groups use allow_extra_args and allow_interspersed_args=False. It returns the deepest context. It stops early if resolve_command returns None for the command.
edge_cases: Callbacks and prompts are not run (resilient parsing)
Unknown subcommand returns the current ctx
interfaces.signature: def _resolve_context(cli: Command, ctx_args: cabc.MutableMapping[str, t.Any], prog_name: str, args: list[str]) -> Context

interfaces.name: _resolve_incomplete
interfaces.behavior: Normalizes '=': `incomplete=='='` becomes ''. `--opt=val` is split, and the name is appended to args. If '--' is not in args and incomplete starts with an option prefix, it returns (ctx.command, incomplete). Otherwise it returns the first Option for which _is_incomplete_option is true. Next it returns the first Argument that is still incomplete. Finally it falls back to (ctx.command, incomplete), which gives subcommand names.
edge_cases: After '--', option-like words are values
Flags and counts never need values
interfaces.signature: def _resolve_incomplete(ctx: Context, args: list[str], incomplete: str) -> tuple[Command | Parameter, str]

interfaces.name: _is_incomplete_argument
interfaces.behavior: True for an Argument that has nargs=-1, or was not given on the command line, or has nargs>1 with fewer values than nargs.
edge_cases: Non-Argument params return False
interfaces.signature: def _is_incomplete_argument(ctx: Context, param: Parameter) -> bool

interfaces.name: _is_incomplete_option
interfaces.behavior: True if param is an Option that is not a flag or count, and the last option-looking arg within nargs positions from the end is in param.opts.
edge_cases: Flags and counts return False
interfaces.signature: def _is_incomplete_option(ctx: Context, args: list[str], param: Parameter) -> bool

cards.error_conventions: The module raises no exceptions deliberately. shell_complete signals failure through return codes: 1 for an unknown shell or instruction, 0 for success. Command._main_shell_completion then calls sys.exit(rv). Abstract methods raise bare NotImplementedError (lines 351 and 373). Missing COMP_WORDS or COMP_CWORD env vars surface as KeyError from os.environ. split_arg_string catches the shlex ValueError internally. BashComplete._check_version reports problems through echo(..., err=True) using gettext `_()` messages. The messages are plain sentences ending in a period, for example "Shell completion is not supported for Bash versions older than 4.4.".

limitations: Completion runs make_context with resilient_parsing=True, so side effects in callbacks are skipped, but any custom shell_complete code still runs on every Tab press.
Bash support is documented as requiring bash >= 4.4. The check only prints a warning when the script is sourced.
